verdicts.reason: Both break the product apart: the cream circle sits clipped in the bottom-left corner, away from the jar. Both also leave the headline small, the 'Out now.' copy tiny, and large dead orange areas. A is worse: its CTA is a tiny, off-centre pill at the bottom edge and the left-aligned text doesn't line up with the centred jar. B's centred CTA is larger and easier to read, though its headline sits only 17px from the left edge.

A: the headline is jammed 17px from the left edge and 'Out now.' is tiny. The jar floats mid-canvas with no background, and its cream circle is clipped in the corner. B shares the clipped circle, tiny subcopy and left-aligned text that ignores the centred jar and CTA. It is slightly better: a more comfortable left margin and a product-to-headline-to-CTA reading order that matches the original.

A: the headline hugs the left edge (17px), 'Out now.' is tiny, and the cream product circle is cut off in the bottom-left corner, apart from the jar. B has the same broken circle and too-small text, plus a big empty band at the top. Its margin and reading order (product, then headline, then CTA) are a little better.

Both use the same fragmented layout. The jar is outline-only, and its cream circle is clipped in the corner. Text is small and left-aligned, while the product and CTA are centred, and there are large dead gaps. A gives the headline a slightly better margin (26px vs 17px) and a clearer top-down order. B jams the headline against the edge.
